title: Target naturality of module cohomology maps for an isomorphism
statement: Let X and Y be schemes, h : X -> Y, G an O_Y-module, F and F′ O_X-modules, phi : G -> h_*F, e : F ≅ F′ and p a natural number. The additive cohomology map moduleCohomologyFMap(h,phi,p), followed by H^p(X,e.hom), equals moduleCohomologyFMap(h,phi followed by h_*(e.hom),p). Cohomology and its h-map are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap].

proof.text: Choose the data C and C′ defining the two canonical maps. Use InjectiveResolution.desc to lift e.hom between the target resolutions and id_G between the source resolutions, respecting augmentations. Scheme module categories have enough injectives, as required for the derived-functor comparisons.

Reuse lift_nat_quasiIso and unique_nat_quasiIso from ModuleCohomologyFMapComparison through a proof-only import all. The first helper lifts the pushforward coefficient descent followed by C′.lambda across C.lambda, producing the lambda homotopy. Compatibility of beta and the augmentation equations identify the composites of the beta square with C.J.ι. The second existing helper reflects homotopy uniqueness after this quasi-isomorphic augmentation, producing the beta homotopy. These helpers already implement extension by zero and K-injective localization; they are not proved again here.

Apply additive global sections and homology to both homotopies. Prove the sections-comparison square componentwise using the sections fields and presheaf naturality. isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality and mapHomologyIso_inv_naturality identify the resolution transports with H^p(e.hom) and id on H^p(G). Cancel the invertible vertical maps and resolution comparisons in the resulting two squares. Unfold ModuleCohomologyFMapData.map and apply this equality to the two canonical choices. The private helper proves the same comparison for any coefficient morphism, without using h-map functoriality or the restriction theorem.

theorem moduleCohomologyFMap_target_iso_naturality {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (h : X ⟶ Y)
    {G : SheafOfModules.{u} Y.ringCatSheaf} {F F' : SheafOfModules.{u} X.ringCatSheaf}
    (φ : G ⟶ (pushforward h).obj F) (e : F ≅ F') (p : ℕ) :
    moduleCohomologyFMap h φ p ≫ (forget₂ _ AddCommGrpCat).map
      ((RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace p).map e.hom) =
      moduleCohomologyFMap h (φ ≫ (pushforward h).map e.hom) p
